name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,449

clue.text: Writer's authentic choral composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the words that follow are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a writer whose choral piece rings true.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'choral composition' looks like a piece of music but is the anagram signal at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical author is a person who writes manuals and documentation, so a kind of professional writer.

clue.text: Balancing act with pedestrian supporting drunk painter?

definitions.note: the act stands for the performer who does it

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it, so it is written second

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
a painter is the rope used to tie up a small boat
a pedestrian is someone on foot

explanation.surface: A walker holds up a tipsy artist as they stagger home.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags painter in its nautical sense: a painter is a boat's mooring line, not an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker is the circus performer whose whole act consists of keeping balance on a high wire.

clue.text: Criminal beside vicar in court

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the first two pieces go within the abbreviation for court

blocks.note: on can mean beside, as in a house on the river
Vic is a familiar shortening of vicar
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A criminal stands next to a clergyman in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is a person found guilty of a crime and serving a sentence, so a criminal.

clue.text: No one in composition of Wagner is Scandinavian

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed in among the composer's name before it is rearranged
a composition is something assembled, so the composer's letters are put together in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody in a Wagner piece comes from Scandinavia, despite all those Nordic gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is one of the Scandinavian countries, so a Norwegian person is a Scandinavian.

clue.text: Allegedly betrays terrorist groups

indicators.note: allegedly means as people say, so the word is judged by how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: to sell someone out is to betray them

explanation.surface: A claim that someone is informing on terror groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrorist networks organise themselves into small independent units known as cells, so each one is a group.

clue.text: Meat company importing Russia's wine

indicators.note: a company importing something brings it inside, so the country's abbreviation goes within the company's

blocks.note: lamb is a meat
RUS is an abbreviation for Russia
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A meat firm brings in Russian wine as a sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Russia only makes the surface read; the abbreviation is RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red Italian wine from the Emilia-Romagna region.

clue.text: Alliance's growth without leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and without it means that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a bunion is a bony growth on the foot

explanation.surface: A political alliance is growing now that it has lost its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'; 'growth' suggests expansion, but it is a swelling at the base of the big toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of parties or states for a common purpose, which is what an alliance is.

clue.text: Description of beer maker's role in book

blocks.note: what a beer maker does, put as a short sentence about him

explanation.surface: A job description for a brewer, written up in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HE BREWS, a two-word description of the brewer's job; whole, it is a book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Hebrews is a book of the New Testament of the Bible.

clue.text: Made an impression casting runes for carer

indicators.note: casting runes means throwing them down to read, so they land in a random order

blocks.note: something that registered made an impression on the mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller casting runes impresses a client looking for a carer.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered nurse is a qualified nurse, one whose job is caring for the sick.

clue.text: Upper class girl embraces New Age leader

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round, so the girl's word goes around the rest

blocks.note: gel is the upper-class drawl of the word girl
N is the abbreviation for new
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A posh young woman takes up New Age beliefs and becomes their figurehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age leader' looks like one phrase, but 'leader' alone is the definition. GEL mimics how a cut-glass English accent says girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a senior army officer who commands troops, a military leader.

clue.text: Report of laddish talk about carrier

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for laddish is taken by its sound
about means turned round, so the word for talk is written back to front

blocks.note: laddish behaviour is typically male
gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: An account of lads' banter about some porter or other.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is a sack in which letters are carried, so it is a carrier for post.

clue.text: Painful sensation expelling a bit of gastric wind

indicators.note: a bit of a word here means just its opening letter
to expel is to throw out, so that letter is removed from the sensation

blocks.note: a twinge is a sudden sharp pain
the first letter of gastric

explanation.surface: Relief from a stomach cramp by passing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' at the end looks like flatulence, completing the surface; it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to wind or coil something around, as a plant twines round a stake.

clue.text: Satire regularly annoys foreigners

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
to anger someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: Satirical humour keeps irritating people from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangers are people from elsewhere who are unknown locally, an older sense close to foreigners.

clue.text: His escort arranged to get leggy birds

indicators.note: something arranged is set out in an order of someone's choosing, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man sets up his escort agency to meet long-legged women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leggy birds' plays on bird as British slang for a young woman; here they are real birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostriches are huge flightless African birds with very long, powerful legs for running.

clue.text: British ship (small) patrols quarter in border work

indicators.note: a ship patrolling an area moves all round it, so the ship's letters surround the compass point

blocks.note: HMS, Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes British naval vessels
east is one of the four quarters of the compass
titch is British slang for a small person, and titchy means tiny

explanation.surface: A small naval vessel patrols part of a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border work' sounds like guarding a frontier, which the ship and patrols back up; it is sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemstitch is a decorative needlework stitch used to finish the hem or border of fabric.

clue.text: Produce problem children

blocks.note: first meaning: to put out or publish
second meaning: a matter of concern
third meaning: offspring, especially in legal wording

explanation.surface: Having awkward kids.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings stand side by side; 'problem children' reads as one phrase, but each word is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to give out, a point in dispute, and a person's descendants, as in dying without lawful offspring.

clue.text: Thereby contributes to sponsorships of actors

indicators.note: the answer contributes some of the letters making up the phrase that follows, so it lies inside it

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sponsor's money funds performers, and so helps the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, so it serves as a formal synonym for therefore or thereby.

clue.text: Corroded part of heat engine

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer is a run of their letters

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A component of a heat engine has rusted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that is eaten away has been worn down by chemical action, which is what corroded means.

clue.text: One of many found in bag of East End criminal

definitions.text: One of many found in bag

blocks.clueFragment: One of many found in bag
blocks.note: first meaning: a scrap of dried leaf inside a teabag
second meaning: Cockney rhyming slang for a thief

explanation.surface: A crook from London's East End with a bag full of loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from London's East End, swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; here the rhyme is with thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A teabag holds many shredded leaves, and in rhyming slang a thief is called by the phrase rhyming with it.

clue.text: The quality of The Who's drummer is a gem

blocks.note: Keith Moon was the drummer in the rock band The Who; with the possessive he gives the first piece
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: Praise for the sound of a famous rock drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as MOON'S TONE: the quality of Keith Moon's playing. The Who were a 1960s British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonstone is a pearly, translucent feldspar cut and polished as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Beat soldiers in the open air

definitions.note: an adjective; the phrase works as one, as in an in-the-open-air concert

blocks.note: to outdo is to beat
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are drilled outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor describes things done or found outside buildings, under the sky rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Gypsum obtained from plant by a research facility

blocks.note: taken as written
a lab is a laboratory, where research is done
an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A mineral sourced from a factory next to a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory or works, which fits gypsum, but it is a garden flower; 'by' puts the laboratory beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained white variety of gypsum carved into ornaments.

clue.text: Address of man in the outskirts of Airedale

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outer letters of the dale are taken
the man is placed in among those outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
bod is British slang for a person or fellow

explanation.surface: Where a man lives on the edge of a Yorkshire valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Airedale is a valley in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is the place where one lives, which is what an abode is.

clue.text: One standing for King and Emperor's queen

blocks.note: R is for Rex, Latin for king
I is for Imperator, Latin for emperor, and the 's is read as is
ER is for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone stands as a candidate for the throne on behalf of the monarch and his empress.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin titles behind the letters on coins and post-boxes: R for Rex, I for Imperator, ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is someone who gets up or stands up, as in an early riser.

clue.text: Joy catches pair leaving wife in bed

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife leaves, so that letter is dropped from the word for pair
to catch something is to hold it, so the word for joy closes around the rest

blocks.note: fun is enjoyment
a pair is two
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Joy finds a couple in bed without the wife: an affair uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a thin Japanese-style mattress used as a bed, often on a folding frame.

clue.text: Look around elsewhere for bar

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word for look is written backwards

blocks.note: a peek is a quick look
someone out is not at home but elsewhere

explanation.surface: Search somewhere else for a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to search for, but it is the verb meaning to exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone out is to prevent their entry, which is what to bar them means.

clue.text: Briefly that tribunal cut short aid

indicators.note: briefly means made short, so the word for that loses its last letter
cut short means the end is chopped off, so the tribunal word loses its final letter

blocks.note: such can mean that, as in such a thing
a tribunal is a court of justice

explanation.surface: Cutting a tribunal short halts legal assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help given in time of need, so it is a formal synonym of aid.

clue.text: Appeal to welcome new student in training

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the student word goes inside the appeal word

blocks.note: recourse is an appeal to someone for help
a fresher is a British first-year university student

explanation.surface: A university appeals for freshers to join its training scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course is a short programme of training that updates skills already learnt.
